title: Cardinality of an injection, at the level of bare counts
statement: Let p and q be decidable predicates and sigma a function. If sigma is injective on the indices below n that p selects, and sends each of them to an index below m that q selects, then countRange p n is at most countRange q m. This is the cross-bound counting INEQUALITY: F:nat-countrange-bij gives the equality but needs a constructive inverse, while an injection alone gives only the bound -- which is exactly what a pigeonhole argument consumes.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.countRange_le_of_injOn : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat) -> ((x7 : AxNat.lt x5 x3) -> ((x8 : Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x5) Bool.true) -> ((x9 : AxNat.lt x6 x3) -> ((x10 : Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x6) Bool.true) -> ((x11 : Eq.{1} AxNat (x2 x5) (x2 x6)) -> Eq.{1} AxNat x5 x6)))))))) -> ((x6 : ((x6 : AxNat) -> ((x7 : AxNat.lt x6 x3) -> ((x8 : Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x6) Bool.true) -> And (AxNat.lt (x2 x6) x4) (Eq.{1} Bool (x1 (x2 x6)) Bool.true))))) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.countRange x0 x3) (AxNat.countRange x1 x4))))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.countRange_le_of_injOn is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.

evidence.supports: The statement says what its name says -- checked at a concrete instance with hand-computed numerals and paired with the specific wrong statement it rules out
evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a THEOREM's statement is not what its name says: a `card_le_of_injOn` with its two `card`s transposed, an `exists_collision` whose pair need not be DISTINCT, or a `pigeonhole` whose strict inequality points the other way would each be admitted, carry an empty axiom footprint, and pass every other row in this ledger. `nat_prelude/finset_pigeonhole_tests.rs` instantiates each statement at a concrete pair of sets whose cardinalities are computed independently, and pairs every positive with the wrong statement it rules out. Three of its controls are the sharper kind, where a hypothesis cannot be DISCHARGED (`infer` must fail) rather than a conclusion merely being false.

notes: The proof is F:nat-countrange-bij's own induction with the inverse tau and the two round-trip equations DELETED, so it reuses count_range_bij.rs's single-point removal apparatus and pays for the removal with Nat.countRange_point_change. Exactly two branches change and both get simpler: the base case n = 0 becomes Nat.zero_le (the bijection's had to refute every selected j < m through tau), and the selected successor branch closes through Nat.succ_le_succ instead of an equality. No arithmetic lemma is needed to line the two spellings up, because add x (sel true) reduces to succ x and add x (sel false) reduces to x by iota-delta -- Nat.add recurses on its RIGHT argument. ADR-1593.
